{{Current events|year=2021|month=02|day=7|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**A [[roadside bomb]] [[explode]]s in [[Dusmareb]], [[Somalia]], killing twelve agents of the [[National Intelligence and Security Agency]], including its local head. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/7/at-least-12-killed-in-central-somalia-roadside-bomb-attack (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020–21 Sudanese–Ethiopian clashes]]
**[[Finnish Foreign Minister]] [[Pekka Haavisto]] arrives in [[Khartoum]] to help reduce tensions between [[Sudan]] and [[Ethiopia]]. He will also visit a [[refugee camp]] containing [[refugee]]s fleeing the [[Tigray War]] and visit Ethiopia after spending time in Sudan. [https://eeas.europa.eu/headquarters/headquarters-homepage/92710/pekka-haavisto-visit-sudan_en (''European Union'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Uttarakhand glacial outburst flood]]
**A glacier breaks off in [[Joshimath]], [[India]], in [[Uttarakhand]]'s [[Chamoli|Chamoli district]] resulting in [[flash flood]]s along the [[Alaknanda River]] and [[Dhauliganga River]]. Eighteen people are found dead and 200 more are feared dead. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-disaster/rescuers-search-for-125-missing-after-glacier-burst-in-indian-himalayas-many-believed-trapped-in-tunnel-idUSKBN2A808I (Reuters)]
*An [[list of earthquakes in the Philippines|earthquake]] of magnitude 6.1 occurs in the southern [[provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Davao del Sur]], [[Philippines]], with damage and aftershocks expected. No casualties have been reported. [https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2021/02/07/2075988/no-official-damage-casualty-yet-63-quake-davao-del-sur (''The Philippine Star'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
*****[[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Rep.]] [[Ron Wright (politician)|Ron Wright]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]-[[Texas|TX]]) dies from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] at the age of 67, thus making him the first member of [[United States Congress|Congress]] to die from the disease. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/rep-ron-wright-has-died-covid-19-his-office-announces-n1257026 (NBC News)]
****The [[United States]] surpasses 27 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.kiro7.com/news/trending/coronavirus-total-us-covid-19-cases-top-27-million-death-toll-swells-past-463000/KMEHWDFYS5ATDLTEBQZM7GQXTI/ (KIRO-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]], [[Lineage P.1]]
*****[[Ontario]] reports [[Canada]]'s first case of the Lineage P.1 variant in a person who travelled from [[Brazil]] to [[Toronto]]. [https://www.cp24.com/news/ontario-s-first-case-of-the-brazil-coronavirus-variant-reported-in-toronto-1.5299343 (CP24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Beatriz Yamamoto Cázarez]] becomes the fifth incumbent member of the [[Congress of the Union]] to die from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/estados/muere-por-covid-la-diputada-y-empresaria-beatriz-yamamoto (''El Universal'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Afghanistan]]
****[[Afghanistan]] receives 500,000 doses of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine]] from [[India]]. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/first-doses-of-covid-19-vaccine-arrive-in-afghanistan-from-india/article33774495.ece (''The Hindu'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] begins a nationwide vaccination programme against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in [[Dhaka]]. [http://www.newsonair.com/News?title=Nationwide-Corona-vaccination-launched-in-Bangladesh&id=409381 (All India Radio)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] receives its first 600,000 doses of the [[Sinopharm]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] from [[China]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/cambodia-covid-19-vaccine-key-ally-china-75738331 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] surpasses 2,000 cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-vietnam-idUSL4N2KD0AQ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
****[[Austria]] tightens its border controls with all neighbouring countries in order to avoid non-essential travel due to the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.thelocal.at/20210207/austria-tightens-border-controls (''The Local Austria'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] approves the use of the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] in the country. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/02/07/hungary-approves-russias-sputnik-v-vaccine-a72853 (''The Moscow Times'')] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[South Africa]] suspends its rollout of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZenenca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] after research finds that the vaccine is less effective against the [[501.V2 variant]] discovered in the country. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-south-africa-halts-rollout-of-astrazeneca-jab-due-to-limited-protection-12211970 (Sky News)] 
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****A limited-size clinical trial in [[Johannesburg]] suggests that the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine is weak against the 501.V2 [[variant of SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/astrazeneca-vaccine-doesnt-protect-against-mild-and-moderate-cases-from-south-africa-strain-11612700385 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*The [[Ministry of Public Health (Democratic Republic of the Congo)|health ministry]] of the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] announces a "resurgence" of the [[Ebola]] virus in the country's eastern side, after it was reported that a woman there died from the disease four days prior. The announcement comes three months after the [[World Health Organization]] declared an end to the [[Kivu Ebola epidemic#2020 Équateur Province outbreak and other regional health issues|Kivu Ebola outbreak]] in the country's [[Province of Équateur|Équateur province]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210207-dr-congo-announces-resurgence-of-ebola-1 (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–United States relations after 1979]]
**Supreme Leader [[Ali Khamenei]] says that the [[United States]] should "lift all sanctions" if it wants to reverse its nuclear steps, saying that [[Iran]] complied with all obligations of the 2015 deal and accuses the United States and European countries of not doing so. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-nuclear-usa/irans-khamenei-u-s-must-lift-sanctions-for-tehran-to-return-to-nuclear-commitments-idUSKBN2A7093?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2018–2021 Haitian protests]]
**The [[Government of Haiti|Haitian government]] says that it has thwarted an attempted [[coup d'état]] against [[President of Haiti|President]] [[Jovenel Moïse]], with at least 23 people arrested. Protesters assert that Moïse's term expires today, however, he claims that his term ends on February 7, 2022; in accordance with the [[Constitution of Haiti|constitution]]. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1393265/attempted-coup-foiled-in-haiti-justice-minister (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Ecuadorian general election]]
**[[Elections in Ecuador|General elections]] occur in [[Ecuador]] to elect the successor of [[President of Ecuador|President]] [[Lenín Moreno]]. Socialist and former aide of President [[Rafael Correa]], [[Andrés Arauz]], is expected to finish in first place, but may face a run-off. [https://www.dw.com/en/polls-open-in-ecuadors-presidential-election/a-56486867 (DW)]
*[[2021 Liechtenstein general election]]
**[[Elections in Liechtenstein|General elections]] occur in [[Liechtenstein]] to elect the 25 members of the [[Landtag of Liechtenstein|Landtag]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/02/07/in-liechtenstein-38-378-of-the-world-s-wealthiest-people-go-to-the-polls (Euronews)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]], aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**Tens of thousands of people protest against the military [[Coup d'état|coup]] in [[Myanmar]]'s largest city [[Yangon]], calling for the release of jailed leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]]. The protests are the largest to occur in the country's history since the 2007 [[Saffron Revolution]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics-protest/biggest-protests-in-myanmar-since-2007-draw-tens-of-thousands-idUSKBN2A702Y?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020 NFL season]], [[Super Bowl LV]]
**The [[2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] win the [[Super Bowl]] following a 31–9 victory against the [[2020 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]], making them the first wildcard team to win the Super Bowl since the [[2010 Green Bay Packers season|2010 Green Bay Packers]] and the [[Super Bowl curse|first]] to win it in [[Raymond James Stadium|their home stadium]]. [[Quarterback]] [[Tom Brady]] is named [[Super Bowl Most Valuable Player Award|Super Bowl MVP]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/american-football/55975394 (BBC)]
**[[Sarah Thomas (American football official)|Sarah Thomas]] becomes the first female [[National Football League|NFL]] [[Official (gridiron football)|official]] to officiate a [[Super Bowl]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/07/sports/football/sarah-thomas-super-bowl-referee.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[2020 FIFA Club World Cup]]
**[[Tigres UANL]] defeats [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras]] 1–0 in the semi-finals, to become the first [[CONCACAF]] team to reach the [[2020 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]] of the [[FIFA Club World Cup]]. [https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/tigres-becomes-first-mexican-team-in-club-world-cup-final/ (AP via ''The Seattle Times'')]
